title: QUIC RFC 9000 NEW_TOKEN Frame Focused Proof
purpose: Describe the bounded RFC 9000 Section 19.7 NEW_TOKEN parser, formatter, duplicate-token, and endpoint-role proof slice.
design_summary: The NEW_TOKEN frame stays centered on the span-backed frame codec and immutable frame view. The parser accepts only the fixed one-byte frame type 0x07, parses Token Length as a QUIC variable-length integer, rejects empty tokens, rejects declared lengths beyond the remaining payload, and consumes exactly the token bytes. The application packet runtime treats malformed client-side receipt as FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR, treats all server-side NEW_TOKEN receipt as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, and refuses to construct outbound NEW_TOKEN payloads from client-role runtimes.
data_and_state_considerations: This slice does not introduce a new token store. Duplicate repair is proven by direct token-byte comparison at the frame seam. Longer-lived token envelope, client reuse, and listener-local replay protection remain owned by the existing Section 8.1 artifact families.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Non-0x07 and non-minimal 0x07 frame-type encodings are rejected by the fixed-type parser.
Truncated Token Length variable-length integers and declared lengths beyond the remaining payload are rejected before a frame view is produced.
A zero-length Token field is invalid at both the codec seam and the client application-packet seam.
Server-side application-packet receipt of NEW_TOKEN closes with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION even when the frame is otherwise malformed.
Client-role runtimes cannot build outbound NEW_TOKEN payloads; server-role runtimes retain the existing token-emission path.
alternatives_considered: Leave S19P7 under broad frame-codec tests; rejected because generated triage required focused requirement-home proof and xrefs.
Move duplicate-token repair into a token cache; rejected because RFC 9000 Section 13.3 already treats duplicate NEW_TOKEN detection as direct frame-content comparison.
Broaden this slice into NEW_TOKEN replay persistence; rejected because listener-local one-time acceptance is already closed separately and cluster or restart persistence remains out of scope.
risks: This proof does not claim persistent replay state across listener restarts or cluster-wide anti-replay coordination.
This proof does not add public token-cache APIs or change the NEW_TOKEN envelope format.
The malformed-frame close proof is bounded to the managed application-packet runtime seam.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers RFC 9000 Section 19.7 NEW_TOKEN parser, formatter, duplicate-token comparison, client send prohibition, client empty-token FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR, and server receive PROTOCOL_VIOLATION behavior for requirements 0001 through 0010 only.
